thread.title: Stocks Rebound; Mnuchin Calls Pullback 'Natural' | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stocks Rebound; Mnuchin Calls Pullback 'Natural' | Investor's Business Daily
text:
U.S. stock indexes led a worldwide stocks rebound as the Nasdaq jumped as much as 2.5% — but in declining volume. If the Nasdaq holds its gain at 2% or more, the advance would be the biggest in six months.
X The stock market, though, remains in a correction, and a price pop after sharp losses is less convincing than those that emerge during a run-up.
The Nasdaq backed off to a 1.7% gain late Friday morning while the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrial average added 1% and 0.7% respectively.
Small caps lagged with the S&P 600 up 0.2%. The Russell 2000 rose 0.6%.
Foreign markets posted smaller gains with the exception of China's markets. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 2.1%. The Shanghai Composite added 0.9%. Other foreign markets capped their gains at 0.5% or less.
Mnuchin On Stock Sell-Off In an interview Friday morning with CNBC, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin called the recent sell-off in stocks " just a natural correction after the markets were up a lot." Mnuchin added that "there's really no new information in the market on the Fed or on trade for that matter."
Stocks appeared accepting of Mnuchin's take. Blue chips were up. Visa ( V ) led the Dow with a 4% thrust. Apple ( AAPL ) followed with a 2% gain.
Bank Shares Struggle As Other Stocks Rebound Three big U.S. banks reported Q3 results. JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) beat the Street's consensus earnings estimate by 4%. Citigroup ( C ) delivered a 3% beat. Wells Fargo ( WFC ) missed by 3%.
The stocks initially rose, and then reversed lower. JPMorgan turned a 2.5% gain in the first five minutes of trade into a 0.3% loss by late morning.
Citigroup trimmed a 4% pop into a 1% gain and then lifted to a 1.6% gain. Wells Fargo advanced almost 4% in the first five minutes of trade and then reversed to a 0.2% loss. A second reversal left it up 1.1%.
Going into Friday's session, the bank sector was down 3.4% for the year, underperforming vs. the S&P 500's 2% gain and the Nasdaq's 6% gain.
Among highly rated stocks, the Innovator IBD 50 Fund ( FFTY ) climbed 3%. The exchange-traded fund pulled back as much as 17% after marking a high Oct. 1. Innovator is 13% off its high now.
